_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'record_schema' (D20, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/twin_validation/l3_release_package_unit_inventory.md D20).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/record_schema.py -- the detector/observable RECORD-SCHEMA + manifest guards
the simulator frontend carries alongside each compiled Stim circuit. It imports NEITHER torch
NOR quimb (dataclass + plain dict/f-string + a lazy `import stim` inside require_stim_circuit),
so EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {}
(the AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim on a torch-less module -> expect ZERO
out_of_scope).
TEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class). RecordSchema is a plain frozen dataclass with NO __post_init__, so
it contributes only its two classmethods (from_stim / from_circuit_ir), two properties
(detector_bit_width / observable_bit_width), and to_manifest. The five module-level functions are
require_frontend_representability / require_stim_circuit / require_matching_schemas /
validate_evaluator_sidecars / b8_manifest_entry. The unit set:
* 5 RecordSchema methods: from_stim / from_circuit_ir / detector_bit_width /
observable_bit_width / to_manifest.
* 5 functions: require_frontend_representability / require_stim_circuit /
require_matching_schemas / validate_evaluator_sidecars / b8_manifest_entry.
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination). Every schema is pinned to its EXACT
manifest/field VALUES vs an INDEPENDENT extraction (StimCounts read straight off the stim.Circuit
for the counts; the CircuitIR's own measurement_keys/detector_names/observable_names for the
names -- NEVER RecordSchema's own accessors). from_circuit_ir is fed a stim circuit whose counts
(m=3,d=2,o=1) DIFFER from the IR's name-lists (mkeys=['m0'], det=[], obs=[]), so the blend is
load-bearing -- a mutant that took names from the wrong source is caught. detector_bit_width /
observable_bit_width are pinned on a hand schema whose num_detectors(3) != num_observables(2) so
the two widths are distinguishable. Every RAISING GUARD is tripped through EVERY route reaching
it with the EXACT message via assert_raises_exact (kills the string wrap/case/None message mutants
a substring match= leaves surviving), AND its happy path is pinned (no-raise / returned value):
* from_circuit_ir: the num_qubits-mismatch raise (exact msg) + the matching happy path.
* require_frontend_representability: the backend-unsupported raise AND the
representability-unsupported raise (each exact) + the all-valid returns-None path.
* require_stim_circuit: the non-stim TypeError (exact) + the stim identity-return happy path.
* require_matching_schemas: the schema-mismatch ValueError (exact, incl. both to_manifest
dict reprs, hand-built independently) + the identical-schema returns-noisy happy path.
* validate_evaluator_sidecars (ISOLATION-CONTRACT relevant -- evaluator-only sidecar gate):
the bad-visibility raise + BOTH second-guard routes (missing-name and missing-path) each
with the exact message + the valid append-and-return-tuple output. The two missing routes
are what kills the `or`->`and` mutant (each trips the raise in orig but NOT under `and`).
* b8_manifest_entry: the negative-bits raise (exact) + the zero-bit-width dict + the normal
dict, plus an L1 property pinning packed_bytes_per_shot == math.ceil(bits/8) over many bits
(kills the (bits+7)//8 arithmetic mutants: +7->N, 7->N, 8->N, //->/).
REACHABILITY (the D13/D18/D19 default-arg / guard-route lesson -- PROBED, not asserted). Every
public function accepts arbitrary input, so each guard is tripped through EVERY input route that
reaches it, and each boolean guard is probed with a non-str non-Sequence value where relevant:
* require_frontend_representability's representability guard is only reached when backend is
VALID (backend='stim'); it is tripped exactly that way (never masked by the backend guard).
* validate_evaluator_sidecars' second guard `"name" not in item or "path" not in item` is
tripped via BOTH operands independently (missing-name-only and missing-path-only, each with a
valid visibility) so the `or` is load-bearing; the visibility `.get("visibility") !=` guard is
tripped on an explicit non-'evaluator_only' visibility AND the valid path exercises the
string-key literal (a mutated "visibility" key -> .get returns None -> raises on a VALID item).
* from_circuit_ir's != comparison is exercised BOTH ways (a 5-qubit stim vs a 3-qubit IR raises;
the matched pair returns).
NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every unit is CPU-pure and every branch is REACHABLE through a
public entry point (checked, not assumed). RecordSchema's from_stim/properties/to_manifest carry
no data-dependent branches; the four guards' raise/return arcs are each tripped both ways.
